title: Marine Parkway–Gil Hodges Memorial Bridge
summary: Everyone believes Mia Holt jumped from the Marine Parkway–Gil Hodges Memorial Bridge. Seven years later, someone secretly logs into her Nimbus account and deletes a folder.

intro.subject: my sister
intro.body:
My sister went missing in 2019. The police decided she killed herself. My mom and I never believed it.

Last night I got a notification: someone signed in to her Nimbus account from a new device. Her account still has my email for recovery. Someone is logging into a dead girl's account seven years later. Why?

The police say it's spam or a random hack and has nothing to do with her case. Please help. I can pay.

mail.subject: the folder
mail.body:
You got into her account? I never could. Mom says Mia kept copies of everything, she was like that since school.

If someone deleted a folder seven years later, there was something in it. Please be careful.

mail.subject: Linden St
mail.body:
The man with the camera across the street from Mia. The police talked to him once and called him a creep. Nobody ever asked to see his recordings.

I don't know if that means anything. I just keep thinking about it.

mail.subject: mom
mail.body:
I asked Mom about Veridia. She cried. They paid her after Mia was gone and made her sign something. She thought it would help with the search.

She never told me. Please don't think badly of her.

officialVersion.status: Suspended (February 2020). Probable suicide, body not found.

timeline.text: Mia leaves home in her car (approximate).
Last signal from her phone, cell tower near Marine Parkway–Gil Hodges Memorial Bridge. Phone goes offline.
Her car is found in the Marine Parkway–Gil Hodges Memorial Bridge parking lot. Bag and keys inside. No phone.

mid.headline: Police reopen review of Mia Holt case
mid.body: NYPD has quietly reopened a review of the 2019 disappearance of Mia Holt. A former Veridia Health employee was questioned but not detained.

message.body: At least something moved. Thank you.

steps.body: I gave everything to the police. Anonymously. The rest is their job.

steps.author: rachel-moore
steps.headline: Mia Holt case reopened seven years later
steps.body: NYPD has reopened the investigation into the disappearance of 24-year-old Mia Holt, who went missing in November 2019. According to sources, investigators received an anonymous package of evidence. A search is underway near Dead Horse Bay. A 38-year-old former employee of Veridia Health has been arrested. The company itself is also under investigation on suspicion of selling medical data of users of its Bloom app.

bonusParagraph.text: Separately, former Veridia CEO Daniel Kerr faces fraud charges for allegedly inflating user numbers to investors.
